reviews.comment: Do not take him
Took honors 151. It was more difficult that I wanted it to be, but Gartland's lectures were good and there were plenty of resources to allow me to get an A.

I took Gartland for honors calc 1. I got an A, but to be honest it took some work. Honestly he was an amazing professor and was very very intrigued in what he was teaching. He's a super nice guy and is pretty young so making jokes in class does not bother him at all. The only thing was by being in honors he expected more and sometimes it was tough.

Dr. Gartland made it very difficult to succeed in this class. All the lectures and homework were designed from an online textbook site, but he wrote his own tests with much harder questions. No extra credit or curve. If one person got an A it was good enough for him. Coming to him was pointless, he would just say the class was supposed to be hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gartland has made Differential Equations simple to understand and unlike other math profs that I had in the past with the exception of one, he is my number one choice. I would definitely recommend him for Differential Equations. You won't be sorry. Show up, you pass. Do the homework, you pass.

Cris Gartland is a great professor. I had him for differential equations (the most Q-dropped course at the university) and he made the subject very doable and actually quite interesting. I recommend taking Dr. Gartland for any other math class.

Prof Gartland is an absolute gem. Probably one of my fav profs at TAMU. He genuinely cares about his students; his tests are fair and he is very approachable. He is very well organized and his teaching style is what worked best for me! He wants the best for you! So best advice is to contact him to schedule office hours. He makes DiffEq easy.

Chris Gartland has been a great professor this semester. Differential Equations seems a little intimidating at first but he does a great job at explaining concepts and also answering questions during class. His exams are really not that bad if you put in some effort to study with the resources he gives.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Chris is a very helpful professor who is extremely passionate about his field. He is always happy to explain something further and teaches very well. I had him for Math 151 and I couldn't have passed without him. Great professor and great guy.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While I did take AP Calculus in high school, which helped a lot, Dr. Gartland was very helpful. His lectures were understandable and the amount of homework given was fair. Quizzes were not extremely difficult and having recitation helped. Although labs with python were not the easiest, being able to work in groups helped!

I took Calc 1 in High School, so this could be why I did not struggle in this course as much. Prof Gartland is really cool and a very good teacher. In my opinion, he explains concepts very well and is very patient with his students when we ask multiple questions. The labs have nothing to do with what we are doing and my TA sucked.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Although Im not an engineering major, I found this class to be not too difficult. Be prepared to rely on your TA a lot, especially for labs and quizzes. Dr. Gartland clearly cared about his students and would stay after class if you needed help. His lectures covered everything needed, so if you attend class and take notes, you wont need to read.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework is Webassign. Weekly print out quizzes. He wasn't bad by any means but also not fantastic. imo taught the stuff but focused a little too much on the theory that Engr students don't need to know. Go to week in review if possible. TEST HEAVY 100% study old common exams for tests. The labs suck; very different from the coding in 102 + bad TA

Professor Gartland is a really great professor! He's super chill, yet knows both the math itself and the theory behind it (AKA he can answer conceptual questions very well). His teaching style is a bit unique, but if you don't understand it in class, he is more than willing to help during office hours and work with you until you get it! STUDY!!

He does the bare minimum that he is paid for. Doesn't really care what his students get and is open about it. Should've put more effort in but I had a lot of family stuff cuz of COVID and a first break-up. Tried to tell him I most likely had COVID (symptoms and my close friend having it), and he said "take my test idc." Never gonna forget that:/
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gartland is really nice prof, he was always helpful during class and his office hours. Talks fast during lectures but keep up and you should be fine. Average amount of homework. Tests were alright as were quizzes. Python labs were the hardest part of this class but your TA handles that. Would take again if I had a better TA.

He makes everything easy to understand and straightforward, and nothing is especially difficult. Labs are a bit tough sometimes but it's possible if you either split it up or work on it all together. Even if you are good at calculus, study for the exams to get an easy A. Despite being new, I do appreciate his attempts to make the class interesting!
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, really easy to learn from. As long as you attend lectures, take notes, and study for exams, you'll do fine in his class.

He is a new professor and you can tell, but aside from his monotonous voice his lectures are very helpful and you are given a lot of tools to succeed in this course. The python labs are a pain, especially if you don't have a good group. The 3 exams you take are pretty simple and get easier if you have prior calc experience. Overall, well organized.
Just a plain professor with a standard class setup. Tests are not that difficult and quizzes are an automatic 100%. The python labs can be tricky.

Nothing super notable or outstanding, but he explains concepts pretty clearly and is easy to approach and talk to if you have questions, which is probably all you could ask for from a professor. Has weekly quizzes, but they were easy 100s because the TAs went over the quiz problems in recitation beforehand.
